evidence.claim: HELIOT is about revealing the unseen by turning light into architecture, material and interaction.
The active experience uses one persistent real-time world containing terrain, reflection basin, gateway, descending passage, underground gallery and exhibit.
The camera crosses the modeled gateway and descends through physical passage geometry rather than using a prerecorded flythrough, image zoom or teleport.
Aperture interaction changes physical diaphragm geometry, optical ray width, semantic readout and exported field-study data.
Reverse scroll reconstructs authored camera and named-node ProductRig states rather than leaving one-way animation residue.
Core HELIOT models and visual media are local/original and the experience has no runtime dependency on remote HDR, photography, AI API, font service, analytics or payment credentials.
Mobile uses the same navigable spatial story with dedicated wider camera framing and preserves chapter access, controls and reduced-motion meaning.
The current HELIOT release uses demand-frame rendering, adaptive quality and a render-cost ledger rather than an unconditional animation loop.
The final field sheet and JSON export preserve visitor-selected finish/aperture state and provide a designed end-state artifact.
The project owner explicitly requested that the latest HELIOT project be completed using the full capabilities of the Forge repository.

unknowns: Safari/WebKit rendering has not been independently verified on a physical Apple device in the current environment.
Physical-device GPU frame-rate performance remains unmeasured; existing render-ledger values are cost observations, not FPS claims.

assumptions.claim: The physical threshold/descent is likely to be more memorable than a later isolated aerial hero pose because it uniquely proves spatial entry and continuity.
